results.summary_before: This design is a 4-bit pipelined Booth multiplier intended for learning purposes. It has been tested in silicon and verified to work correctly for all input pairs, with pipelining functioning as expected. results.summary_before: This design is a multi-mode clock with a four-digit seven-segment display. It uses registers to divide the clock and combinational logic to convert binary to decimal for display, with the bottom 8 bits of the counter available on bidirectional outputs. The counting speed can be adjusted by setting the inputs to program a 24-bit compare register, allowing the counter to increment at different rates. It requires an external seven-segment display and a 10MHz clock source.

results.summary_before: This module provides a PWM generator on output pin 7 and a PWM reader on input pin 7, with the generator duty cycle set by input pins [6:0] and the reader output reflected on output pins [6:0]. The PWM period is assumed to be 20 ms with duty cycle adjustable between 1 ms and 2 ms, suitable for servo control. An SPI interface allows configuration and read/write operations when enabled, and the design can be tested by looping back the generated PWM signal to the input. It requires a development kit and optionally an oscilloscope and signal generator for testing, and is notable for combining PWM input and output with SPI configurability.
